jurisdiction.name: Ukraine
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Ukraine governs AI through soft law. The Cabinet's 2020 Concept for the Development of AI and its action plans set the policy framework; the digital transformation ministry's 2023 bottom-up regulation roadmap and 2024 White Paper lead towards a law aligned with the EU AI Act, for which no bill has yet been published. The ministry has issued sectoral recommendations, including for the media and for public servants' use of AI, and put a draft AI Development Strategy to 2030 to public consultation in June 2026.
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026, mainly from the digital transformation ministry's and the Cabinet's websites. The national legislation portal stopped responding after two documents, and the education ministry's and several regulators' sites could not be accessed, so the data protection law, the Convention 108 ratification law and several sectoral recommendations could not be read; the review also hit a search limit. As a country of over 20 million people with fewer than 10 records, Ukraine is marked for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.official_title: Про схвалення Концепції розвитку штучного інтелекту в Україні
instruments.english_title: On approval of the Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine (Cabinet of Ministers Order No. 1556-r of 2 December 2020)
instruments.current_status: In force (zakon.rada.gov.ua: 'чинний', current edition of 29.12.2021, amended by Cabinet Order No. 1787-r). Implementation is planned to 2030. The draft Cabinet order on the AI Development Strategy to 2030 put to consultation on 15 June 2026 proposes to repeal this order and its action plans; not yet adopted as of 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: Cabinet order approving Ukraine's AI Concept, which defines artificial intelligence and sets the aims, principles and tasks of state AI policy to 2030 across priority areas (education and training, science, economy, cybersecurity, information security, defence, public administration, legal regulation and ethics, justice). It identifies problems such as the absence of AI legal regulation and of common ethical approaches, and instructs the Ministry of Digital Transformation with other central executive bodies to prepare an implementation action plan within three months.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ukraine's current framework AI policy document; the basis for the 2021-2024 action plan and the draft AI Strategy to 2030.

instruments.english_title: On approval of the action plan for implementing the Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine for 2021-2024 (Cabinet of Ministers Order No. 438-r of 12 May 2021)
instruments.current_status: Adopted 12 May 2021; amended by Cabinet Order No. 649-r of 25.07.2023. Its 2021-2024 period has ended; a follow-up 2025-2026 action plan (reported as Order No. 457-r of 9 May 2025) could not be read on the legislation portal (see leads). The draft AI Strategy to 2030 (June 2026) proposes repealing the Concept's action plans.
instruments.summary: Cabinet order approving the 2021-2024 action plan for the AI Concept, listing measures with responsible bodies, deadlines and indicators, starting with preparing a Cabinet act approving a concept for an AI development bill (Ministry of Digital Transformation, Q2 2021), AI awareness campaigns in schools and international research cooperation. Ministries and central executive bodies must implement the plan and report annually by 15 January to the Ministry of Digital Transformation, which reports to the Cabinet by 15 February.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Operational plan for the 2020 AI Concept; assigns AI tasks to individual ministries.

instruments.english_title: Draft Cabinet of Ministers order 'On approval of the Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine until 2030 and approval of the operational action plan for its implementation in 2026-2028'
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
instruments.current_status: Consultation notice published by the Ministry of Digital Transformation on 15.06.2026; comments accepted until 30 June 2026. The Ministry's consultation report (one participant, the TELAS telecom operators' association) is published with the draft, the explanatory note and the 2026-2028 operational plan. Not adopted by the Cabinet as of 2026-10-13 (no adopted order found).
instruments.summary: Draft Cabinet order, put to public consultation by the Ministry of Digital Transformation, that would approve an AI Development Strategy to 2030 with four strategic goals (accelerating AI adoption, developing and widening access to core AI technologies, securing the foundations for AI development, and effective governance for fast and responsible AI adoption) and a 2026-2028 operational plan. The strategy text calls for aligning Ukrainian law with the EU AI Act and designating an AI regulator for market surveillance meeting EU effectiveness and independence criteria; the draft order would repeal the 2020 AI Concept and its action plans.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Proposed successor to the 2020 AI Concept; would set Ukraine's AI governance direction to 2030.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
instruments.current_status: Document dated 'Червень 2024' (June 2024) and marked 'Версія для консультацій'. The National Bank of Ukraine's AI discussion paper (2026) states the Ministry published the White Paper on 26.06.2024. The draft AI Strategy to 2030 (June 2026) carries forward the EU AI Act alignment goal; no AI law adopted as of 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: Consultation version of the Ministry of Digital Transformation's approach to AI regulation, proposing a two-stage 'bottom-up' approach: first, voluntary tools to prepare business and the state (regulatory sandbox, an AI human-rights impact assessment methodology, sectoral recommendations, voluntary codes of conduct, labelling), then a law analogous to the EU AI Act. It states it is an analytical material and not a public-policy analytical document under the Law on Law-Making Activity.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sets out the Ministry's stated pathway to an EU-aligned AI law.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
instruments.current_status: Published by the Ministry of Digital Transformation on 24 January 2024 (news page), developed with the NGO Digital Security Lab, the Expert Committee on AI Development and contributions from the National Council of Television and Radio Broadcasting and the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy. instruments.summary: Sectoral recommendations, part of the AI regulation roadmap, for media using AI at stages from data collection to content creation and audience interaction. They call for transparency about AI use, clear separation of human-authored and AI-generated content, human review and priority of the human role, guidance on choosing AI systems and checking AI-generated content, and media self-regulation.

instruments.summary: Guidance, part of the AI regulation roadmap, on how public servants should adopt and responsibly use AI tools in their work, with attention to personal-data protection (including sensitive data), confidentiality, cyber hygiene, human rights and the general rules of ethical conduct for civil servants and local self-government officials. It advises weighing risks before using a given AI tool or platform and notes that AI use in public service will be regulated through transposition of the EU AI Act.
